xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NatureAndDetailsOfTheActionTak: Food Safety Officer have lifted the sample of Sundrop Peanut Butter (200gm) from M/s. Q-1/0523/2016 dated 01-March-2016, It was alleged by the said report that the sample is misbranded since the size of green colour filled circle of Veg logo is less than 3 mm against the required size of 3 mm. On 24-April-2018 the Addition Judicial/District Magis-trate, Dehradun, passed an Order and imposed a penalty of Rs. 1, 90,000/- on the Company in total (Rs. 40,000 on nominee, Mr. R S Chandersekhar and Rs. 1,50,000/- on ATFL). We have filed an appeal bearing no. 91/2018 against the order dated 24-April-2018 before Food Safety Appellate Tribunal, Ghandhinagar. On 27-Jan-2025, the FSAT, Ghandhinagar has dismissed the appeal filed by Company. Thereaby confirmed the order passed by the Adjudicating Officer & Residential Additional Collector, Surat.

xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: No Change since Last Disclosure. Assistant Commisioner issued assesmsnet order demanding INR.3.68 crores of entry tax on edible oils imported in to Rajasthan for manufcturing /refining. Aggrieved by the assessment for demand, company appealed to the Deputy Commissioner (Appeals), Jaipur, who ruled in favor of the company on May 9, 2006, quashing the entry tax, interest, and penalty. The department challenged the DC (Appeals) order at the Rajasthan Tax Board. On August 11, 2023, the Tax Board partly allowed the department's appeal, restoring the entry tax and interest but upholding the quashing of the penalty. Company filed a revision petition against the Tax Board’s order with the Rajasthan High Court on October 13, 2023. Following a stay hearing on October 20, 2023, the High Court ordered company to deposit ₹10 lakhs per year for 2002-03 and 2003-04 (₹20 lakhs total) and scheduled final disposal for January 4, 2024. Hearing adjourned and the matters are next listed before the Court on 21.02.2025. Separately, the Assistant Commissioner, Anti-Evasion, Jaipur, filed a revision petition with the High Court to challenge the Tax Board’s decision to quash the penalty. Based on the Tax Board’s decision, the Assistant Commissioner issued a demand order for INR.3.98 crores on October 3, 2023, including updated interest. ATFL filed appeal against this order before the first Appellate Authority. Appeallate Authority remand back the case to Assistant Commissioner.
